summary:
[  edit  ]
The Render  TOP  is used to render all 3D scenes in TouchDesigner. You need to give it a  Camera  object and a  Geometry  object as a minimum.
The Geometry object needs to have a  Material  assigned to it. Materials can be pre-packaged ones like the  Phong  material, or they can be OpenGL GLSL shaders. All textures and bump maps in TouchDesigner materials are TOPs, i.e. files must be read in via  Movie File In TOPs .
Rendering  in TouchDesigner ties in nicely with compositing via the Render  TOP  and all other TOPs.
The Render  TOP  renders in many RGBA and single-channel formats, in 8-bit fixed-point up to to 32-bit floating point per pixel component.
It can render transparent surfaces correctly using Multi-Pass Depth Peeling. See below: Order Independent Transparency.
Multiple Cameras: The Render  TOP  is able to render multiple cameras (more quickly than separately) in a single node. You specify multiple cameras in one Camera parameter, and use Render Select  TOP  to pull out those camera results. This feature is even faster on GPUs that support  Multi-Camera Rendering .
Multiple Images out: The Render  TOP , working with the GLSL MATs, can output multiple image at arbitrary formats, through the Images page.
See also  Rendering , all the articles in the  Rendering Category , the  Render Pass TOP , and the troubleshooting page  Why is My Render Black .
NOTE: If you are doing non-realtime  GPU -intensive renders (ones that take multiple seconds to render a single  SOP ), see the note in Windows  GPU  Driver Timeouts in the  Movie File Out TOP .

parameters.label: Camera(s)
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: Specifies which  Cameras  to look through when rendering the scene. You can specify multiple cameras and retrieve each camera image using the Render Select  TOP .

parameters.label: Multi-Camera Hint
parameters.name: multicamerahint
parameters.description: ⊞  - Helps the Render  TOP  optimize rendering when multiple cameras are used. Controls the  Multi-Camera Rendering  behavior for this node.

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: automatic
parameters.description: The node will decide based on the  GPU  and setup if  Multi-Camera Rendering  can be used and enable it if possible. Currently Multi-Camera rendering works for 2D and Cube Map renders on supported GPUs. For 2D renders multiple cameras can not be rendered in a single pass if their 'Camera Light Mask' parameters don't result in the same lights being used in the scene. Use of Depth Peeling or Order Independent Transparency will also disable Multi-Camera rendering.

parameters.label: Off (One Pass Per Camera)
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Forces Multi-Camera Render to be disabled, so each camera is rendered one pass at a time.

parameters.label: X-Offset Stereo Cameras
parameters.name: stereocameras
parameters.description: Should be set only if the pair of cameras have transform/projection matrices that result in a difference only in the X-axis after being applied, as is the case for most VR headsets. Other differences between the cameras such as FOV, near/far plane etc will be ignored, and the values form the first camera will be used. This hint allows the  TOP  to run faster for this particular case, when appropriate hardware is available.

parameters.label: Geometry
parameters.name: geometry
parameters.description: Specifies which  Geometry  will be included in the rendered scene. You can use  Pattern Matching  to specify objects using patterns. Example:  geo* ^geo7  will render all Geometry components whose names start with  geo  except  geo7 .

parameters.label: Lights
parameters.name: lights
parameters.description: Specifies which  Lights  will be used to render the scene. You can use  Pattern Matching  here as well.

parameters.label: Anti-Alias
parameters.name: antialias
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the level of anti-aliasing in the scene. Setting this to higher values uses more graphics memory.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.name: bgcolor
parameters.description: ⊞  - This is combined with the  Camera COMP 's Background Color to determine the final Background Color of the render.

parameters.label: Pre
parameters.description: Multiply RGB by Alpha    premultrgbbyalpha  -

parameters.label: Render Mode
parameters.name: rendermode
parameters.description: ⊞  - You can render different projections:  normal 2D, Cube Map, Fish Eye (180), or Dual Paraboloid. The Cube Map renders 6 views as needed for environment maps in the  Phong MAT  and  Environment Light COMP .

parameters.label: 2D
parameters.name: render2d
parameters.description: The standard 2D render mode.

parameters.label: Cube Map
parameters.name: cubemap
parameters.description: Does 6 renders, each with 90 degree FOV. The camera is automatically turned to face down each of the 6 axis, with the -Z axis being where the camera is facing to start.

parameters.label: Fish-Eye (180)
parameters.name: fisheye180
parameters.description: A single 2D render that warps the projection so it renders 180 degree FOV in all directions from where the camera is pointing (90 to each side). Since this render doesn't preserve straight lines, geometry that has large polygons that cover a lot of the viewport will suffer from artifacts. Well tesselated geometry is best for this mode.

parameters.label: Dual Paraboloid
parameters.name: dualparaboloid
parameters.description: Similar to Fisheye, but renders twice at 180 degrees, once forward and once backwards. The projection isn't the same as fisheye either. This is a legacy mode that isn't currently consumed by anything in TouchDesigner, but there are articles online that discuss how to sample from it.

parameters.label: UV Unwrap
parameters.name: uvunwrap
parameters.description: A 2D render that uses the UV coordinates of the geometry to unwrap it across the output image.

parameters.label: Cube Map (Omnidirectional Stereo)
parameters.name: cubemapods
parameters.description: This mode renders a stereo pair (two eyes) of cubemaps that can be used to record out stereo 360 videos. You can obtain the second eye's output by using a  Render Select TOP  and selecting Camera Index=1. The  Camera COMP 's IPD Shift parameter is used here to offset each eye viewport.

parameters.label: Positive Sides
parameters.name: posside
parameters.description: ⊞  - When Render Mode is Cube Map, specify which sides if the cube map are rendered, +X, +Y, or +Z.

parameters.label: Negative Sides
parameters.name: negside
parameters.description: ⊞  - When Render Mode is Cube Map, specify which sides if the cube map are rendered, -X, -Y, or -Z.

parameters.label: UV Unwrap  SOP  Coord
parameters.name: uvunwrapcoord
parameters.description: ⊞  - When Render Mode is UV Unwrap Coord, for SOPs this selects which Texture Layer coordinates the rendering is done to.

parameters.label: UV Unwrap POP Coord  Attribute
parameters.name: uvunwrapcoordattrib
parameters.description: When Render Mode is UV Unwrap Coord, for POPs this should be the name of the texture coordinate attribute rendering is done to.

parameters.label: Transparency
parameters.name: transparency
parameters.description: ⊞  - Helps to render transparent geometry in proper depth order. More in-depth discussion available in the   Transparency article .

parameters.label: Sorted Draw with Blending
parameters.name: sortedblending
parameters.description: https://docs.derivative.ca/Transparency#Sorting_Geometry_Objects

parameters.label: Order Independent Transparency
parameters.name: orderind
parameters.description: https://docs.derivative.ca/Transparency#Order-Independent_Transparency

parameters.label: Alpha-to-Coverage
parameters.name: alphatocoverage
parameters.description: https://docs.derivative.ca/Transparency#Alpha-to-Coverage

parameters.label: Depth Peel
parameters.name: depthpeel
parameters.description: Depth peeling is a technique used as part of Order-Independent Transparency, but this parameter allows you to use it in a different way. This parameter enables rendering depth-peels, but without combining all the layers using blending to create order independent transparency. Instead is keeps all the layers separate and they can be retrieved using a  Render Select TOP . Depth peeling is done by first rendering rendering geometry normally and saving that image and depth. Then another render is done but the closest pixels that were occluded by the previous pass are written to the color buffer instead. This can be done multiple times, each time peeling back farther into the scene. If you are rendering a sphere the first render will be the outside of the sphere, and the second peel layer will be the back-inside of the sphere.

parameters.label: Transparency/Peel Layers
parameters.name: transpeellayers
parameters.description: Number of passes the renderer will use when  Order Independant Transparency  is turned on.

parameters.label: Render
parameters.name: render
parameters.description: Enables rendering; 1 = on, 0 = off.

parameters.label: Render  Pulse
parameters.name: renderpulse
parameters.description: The the 'Render' toggle above is Off, click this to render a sinlge frame.

parameters.label: Dither
parameters.name: dither
parameters.description: Dithers the rendering to help deal with banding and other artifacts created by precision limitations of 8-bit displays.

parameters.label: Color Output Needed
parameters.name: coloroutputneeded
parameters.description: This is an optimization if you don't actually need the color result from this pass. Turning this off avoids a copy from the offscreen render buffer to the  TOP 's texture. When anti-aliasing is enabled, turning this off will also avoid 'resolving' the anti-aliasing.

parameters.label: Draw Depth Only
parameters.name: drawdepthonly
parameters.description: This will cause the render to only draw depth values to the depth buffer. No color values will be created.  To make use of the depth buffer, use the  Depth TOP .

parameters.label: # of Color Buffers
parameters.name: numcolorbufs
parameters.description: Any shader you write can output to more than one RGBA buffer at a time. For GLSL 3.3+ you would use the layout(location = 1) specifier on an out variable in the pixel shader to write to the 2nd buffer. In GLSL 1.2 instead of writing to  gl_FragColor  in your shader, you write to  gl_FragData[i]  where i is the color buffer index you want to write the value to.

parameters.label: Allow Blending for Extra Buffers
parameters.name: allowbufblending
parameters.description: Controls if blending (as enabled by the  MAT  common page setting) will be enabled for extra buffers beyond the first one. Often the extra buffers are used to write other types of information such as normals or positions, where blending wouldn't be desirable.

parameters.label: Depth Buffer Format
parameters.name: depthformat
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use either a 24-bit Fixed-Point or 32-bit Floating-Point depth buffer (single channel image).

parameters.label: Cull Face
parameters.name: cullface
parameters.description: ⊞  - Front Faces, Back Faces, Both Faces, Neither. Will cause the render to avoid rendering certain polygon faces depending on their orientation to the camera. Refer to  Back-Face Culling  for more information.

parameters.label: Override  Material
parameters.name: overridemat
parameters.description: This allows you to specify a material that will be applied to every Geometry that is rendered in the Render  TOP . It is useful for pre-processing passes where we are outputting information about the geometry rather then lighting them and outputting RGB.

parameters.label: Polygon  Depth Offset
parameters.name: polygonoffset
parameters.description: This feature pushes the polygons back into space a tiny fraction. This is useful when you are rendering two polygons directly ontop of each other and are experiencing  Z-Fighting . Refer to  Polygon Depth Offset  for more information. This is also an important feature when doing shadows.

parameters.label: Offset Factor
parameters.name: polygonoffsetfactor
parameters.description: Adds an offset to the Z value that depends on how sloped the surface is to the viewer.

parameters.label: Offset Units
parameters.name: polygonoffsetunits
parameters.description: Adds a constant offset to the Z value.

parameters.label: Display Overdraw
parameters.name: overdraw
parameters.description: This feature visually shows the overdraw in the scene. Refer to the  Early Depth-Test  article for more information. In particular the Analyzing Overdraw section.

parameters.label: Overdraw Limit
parameters.name: overdrawlimit
parameters.description: This value quantizes the outputted color value to some # of overdraws. Refer to the  Early Depth-Test  for more information.

parameters.label: Cropping here occurs using the projection matrix. It reduces the amount of the output render that is visible, without changing the resolution. It's particuarly useful to create sub
parameters.description: portion of an overall render in different buffers, such as for rendering across multiple instances of TouchDesigner. Be careful to set the aspect ratio of the Render  TOP  to match the 'real' aspect of the overall output image, not the aspect of this subsection. Otherwise the projection will be stretched incorrectly.

parameters.label: Crop Left
parameters.name: cropleft
parameters.description: Positions the left edge of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Crop Left Unit
parameters.name: cropleftunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Crop Right
parameters.name: cropright
parameters.description: Positions the right edge of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Crop Right Unit
parameters.name: croprightunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Crop Bottom
parameters.name: cropbottom
parameters.description: Positions the bottom edge of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Crop Bottom Unit
parameters.name: cropbottomunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Crop Top
parameters.name: croptop
parameters.description: Positions the top edge of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Crop Top Unit
parameters.name: croptopunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Vector
parameters.name: vec
parameters.description: Sequence of uniform name and value pairs.

parameters.label: Uniform Name
parameters.name: vec0name
parameters.description: The uniform name, as declared in the shader.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: vec0value
parameters.description: ⊞  - The value to assign the vector uniform.

parameters.label: Uniform Name
parameters.name: uni0name
parameters.description: The uniform name, as declared in the shader.

parameters.label: Sampler
parameters.name: sampler
parameters.description: Sequence of sampler parmaeters, including uniform name,  TOP  reference, and sampling parameters.

parameters.label: Sampler Name
parameters.name: sampler0name
parameters.description: This is the sampler name that the GLSL program will use to sample from this  TOP . The samplers need to be declared as the same dimensions as the  TOP  (sampler2D for a 2D  TOP , sampler3D for 3D  TOP ).

parameters.label: TOP
parameters.name: sampler0top
parameters.description: ⊞  - This is the  TOP  that will be referenced by the above sampler name above it.

parameters.label: Image
parameters.name: image
parameters.description: A sequence of parameters to control image outputs available for the GLSL MATs.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: image0name
parameters.description: The uniform name for the image.

parameters.label: Array Length
parameters.name: image0arraylength
parameters.description: If this value is 1 or greater, then the uniform is declared as an array and should be accessed using []. If this is 0 then it is not an array.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: image0res
parameters.description: ⊞  - The resolution the image should be.

parameters.label: Format
parameters.name: image0format
parameters.description: ⊞  - The pixel format the image should be allocated as.

parameters.label: Use Output
parameters.name: useoutput
parameters.description: Use the same pilxe format that the Render TOPs main texture is set to be.

parameters.label: sRGB 8
parameters.description: bit fixed (RGBA)   srgba8fixed  -

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: image0type
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify what type of texture to create with the image output.

parameters.label: Depth
parameters.name: image0depth
parameters.description: Set the depth when output Type is 2D Texture Array or 3D Texture.

parameters.label: Access
parameters.name: image0access
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how the output textures will be accessed. If the textures will be read from (such as using values generated by other shader executions within the same frame), then the access should be changed to Read-Write instead of Write Only.

parameters.label: Read
parameters.description: Write   readwrite  -

parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input

parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)

parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)

parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)

Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.description: DCI-P3  color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim"  color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.description: Display-P3  color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.description: 1  -  ACES 2065-1  (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg
parameters.description: ACEScg  (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.name: useparent
parameters.description: Will use the  Reference  White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use  Parent ' selected, then 'UI  Reference  White' will be used.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: UI
parameters.name: ui
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI  Reference  White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.label: resx
parameters.description: Horizontal resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: resy
parameters.description: Vertical resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: aspectx
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: aspecty
parameters.description: Vertical aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: depth
parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this  TOP  contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this  TOP .

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

localNotes.excerpt: # Evaluación de mejoras inspiradas en TWOZERO TWOZERO se describe como un toolkit nativo para TouchDesigner con: - Generación por IA - Librería curada de componentes - Sincronización en la nube - Herramientas de producción - Integración en UI y sin “wrappers” externos ## Qué se puede integrar en este MCP (sin depender de TWOZERO) - **Librería curada de patrones (component library)** Crear un catálogo de “recetas” reproducibles (render, instancing, feedback loops, POP sims, GLSL) como: - skills en Markdown (`touchdesigner/skills/*`) - prompts maestros (`docs/06-master-prompts.md` o carpeta `prompts/`) - scripts Python idempotentes (crear/actualizar redes sin duplicar) - **No ensuciar el proyecto (non-invasive)** Convenciones sistemáticas: - encapsular sistemas en `baseCOMP`/`geoCOMP` - nodos “I/O estándar” (`in*`, `out*`, `null*`) - layout determinístico (`nodeX/nodeY`) - nombres consistentes y prefijos por

da primitiva tiene una lista de vértices. Un vértice es un índice que apunta a un punto específico en la lista de puntos. Los vértices también pueden tener atributos. • Una lista de primitivas: Son conjuntos de puntos que definen una forma geométrica. Los tipos de primitivas en POPs incluyen Punto (1 punto), Línea (2 puntos), Tira de Líneas (1 o más puntos), Triángulo (3 puntos) y Quad (4 puntos). Las primitivas también pueden tener atributos, como Color. Los POPs se renderizan utilizando el Render TOP en TouchDesigner. Son considerados un reemplazo y una "re-concepción" de la familia de operadores SOPs (Surface Operators), ofreciendo un flujo de trabajo más moderno que combina lo mejor de SOPs, CHOPs y TOPs.
